identity.title: Berberine nanostructures attenuate ss-catenin, a key component of epithelial mesenchymal transition in lung adenocarcinoma.

content.abstract: Lung cancer (LC) is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths globally. It accounts for more than 1.9 million cases each year due to its complex and poorly understood molecular mechanisms that result in unregulated cell proliferation and metastasis. beta-Catenin is a developmentally active protein that controls cell proliferation, metastasis, polarity and cell fate during homeostasis and aids in cancer progression via epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Therefore, inhibition of the beta-catenin pathway could attenuate the progression of LC. Berberine, an isoquinoline alkaloid which is known for its anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory properties, demonstrates poor solubility and bioavailability. In our study, we have encapsulated berberine into liquid crystalline nanoparticles to improve its physiochemical functions and studied if these nanoparticles target the beta-catenin pathway to inhibit the human lung adenocarcinoma cell line (A549) at both gene and protein levels. We observed for the first time that berberine liquid crystalline nanoparticles at 5 microM significantly attenuate the expression of the beta-catenin gene and protein. The interaction between berberine and beta-catenin was further validated by molecular simulation studies. Targeting beta-catenin with berberine nanoparticles represents a promising strategy for the management of lung cancer progression.
